section_summary: This section covers diplomatic and intelligence reporting on the February 26 Incident (1936 military insurrection in Tokyo) and its immediate political aftermath. It includes cables and memoranda from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and State Department officials analyzing the suppression of the revolt, Prime Minister Okada's survival, and Koki Hirota's formation of a new cabinet under military influence. Additional reports document international reactions and commentary from Moscow, Geneva, Berlin, Paris, and Lima concerning Japan's political instability, agrarian grievances, and future foreign policy toward China and the Soviet Union.

subfiles.about: Fragment of a received naval/diplomatic telegram concerning early reports of events in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Contains fragmentary received text of a telegram apparently transmitted via naval channels concerning initial developments during the Tokyo military coup. The readable portions contain transmission markers and codes.
subfiles.title: Fragmentary Telegram on Tokyo Events

subfiles.about: Naval attache message reporting military coup, political assassinations, and press censorship in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Peiping Naval Attaché reports a Tokyo military coup with political assassinations and total press censorship, relayed priority to Naval Operations.
subfiles.title: Peiping Naval Attache Telegram on Military Coup d'Etat

subfiles.about: State Department instructions to Embassy Tokyo requesting an authoritative account of the coup, Okada's fate, and insurgent leaders.
subfiles.summary: State instructs Tokyo to compile an authoritative coup report, clarifying conflicting accounts about Okada's survival, actions against mutineers, and rebel leaders' fate.
subfiles.title: State Department Instruction No. 28 to Tokyo

subfiles.about: Grew reports that a comprehensive pouch despatch is being prepared, though official details remain hampered by censorship.
subfiles.summary: Grew says the Embassy is compiling official statements and leaflets for a March pouch report, cautioning full details will take time under continued censorship.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 57 on Pouch Report Compilation

subfiles.about: Grew reports Saionji's arrival in Tokyo to consult leaders on a new cabinet while the Okada cabinet serves provisionally.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Saionji arrived to consult leaders on the next cabinet; press demands a strong national government while Okada's cabinet continues provisionally.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 56 on Saionji's Consultations

subfiles.about: Grew reports unconfirmed news agency accounts that Prince Konoye has been asked to form a cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports unconfirmed news that Prince Konoye was instructed to form a cabinet, which officials indicated was likely trustworthy.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 58 on Prince Konoye

subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum analyzing the origins, extremist motivations, and immediate impact of the Tokyo coup.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE: SKH/EJL)
subfiles.summary: FE memo reviews initial assassination reports, situating the revolt within six years of recurring radical military action against constitutional restraint.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on the Military Coup in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum reviewing the surrender of insurgents, Okada's survival, and political consequences.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE: SKH/ZMK)
subfiles.summary: Memo summarizes Okada's surprise survival and surrendering troops, warning Takahashi's death weakens cabinet resistance and strengthens military dominance over domestic and China policy.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on the Military Coup Developments

subfiles.about: Grew reports that Prince Konoye has declined the Imperial command to form a cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Grew cables that Konoye declined the Premiership after consulting Saionji.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 59 on Konoye Declining Premiership

subfiles.about: Grew reports that Foreign Minister Hirota has received the Imperial command to form a cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Hirota received Imperial instructions to form a cabinet and is conferring with leaders.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 60 on Hirota Commanded to Form Cabinet

subfiles.about: Grew reports Hirota's difficulties with the army and key appointments to the Imperial Household.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Hirota's cabinet-building hit army difficulties, noting Yuasa's and Matsudaira's appointments as Privy Seal Keeper and Household Minister.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 61 on Hirota's Cabinet Difficulties

subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum discussing the standoff with mutineers and potential outcomes.
subfiles.summary: Memo written during the standoff assesses that any compromise settlement, not just forceful suppression, will increase military leverage over the state.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on the Military Coup in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull's memorandum of conversation with Ambassador Saito regarding trade policy and the Tokyo uprising.
subfiles.summary: Hull records Saito conveying Hirota's thanks and arguing the rebellion reflected farmer/small-business grievances against big business, not ideology, explaining senior generals' resignations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Secretary Hull and Ambassador Saito

subfiles.about: Written message from Hirota expressing gratitude for American condolences following the Tokyo assassinations.
subfiles.summary: Hirota conveys Japan's sincere gratitude to Hull for American condolences following the recent assassinations.
subfiles.title: Message from Foreign Minister Hirota to Secretary Hull

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting Grew's report on Japanese police protection assigned to foreign ambassadors.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Tokyo telegram 55 reports mutineers surrendered and Home Office proposing plainclothes guards for American, Soviet, and British ambassadors.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Protection of Foreign Ambassadors

subfiles.about: Confidential report from a Japanese General Staff officer to Military Attache Crane on the coup and army politics.
subfiles.summary: A General Staff briefing described rebels as misled enlisted men, confirmed officer suicides/investigations, explained senior resignations (Araki, Mazaki, Minami), and Terauchi's demand for a reformist, non-political cabinet.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 63 on General Staff Briefing to Military Attache

subfiles.about: Ambassador Bullitt reports Soviet assessments by Litvinov and Tukhachevsky regarding the Tokyo crisis.
subfiles.summary: Bullitt reports Litvinov saw anti-war elements in control, but Tukhachevsky warned displaced extremists like Araki/Mazaki would be more dangerous unseated, leaving peace precarious.
subfiles.title: Moscow Telegram No. 80 on Soviet Reactions to Tokyo Coup

subfiles.about: Grew reports the successful formation and composition of Hirota's cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that Hirota has formed a cabinet, temporarily retaining the Foreign Affairs portfolio after the army rejected Yoshida. Key cabinet appointments are reviewed, including Baba (Finance), Terauchi (War), Nagano (Navy), Ushio (Home Affairs and Education), and Hayashi (Justice), noting the cabinet's broad party and administrative balance.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 65 on Formation of Hirota Cabinet

subfiles.about: Grew's confidential analysis of the social and economic root causes of the rebellion and future cabinet challenges.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew analyzes the February 26 insurrection as an outgrowth of severe domestic agrarian distress and popular resentment against plutocratic political influence. He asserts that the military seeks a 'new deal' supported by the public, warns that the Hirota cabinet must address these economic issues to survive army pressure, and cautions that Hirota's ability to restrain the army in China and Manchuria remains untested. A paraphrased copy is included on pages 329-330.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 66 on Domestic Causes of the Insurrection

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting Lima press interviews with the Japanese Minister and a Japanese newspaper editor on the coup.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Lima (R. M. de Lambert)
subfiles.summary: Secretary of Embassy de Lambert transmits translations and clippings from the Lima daily La Prensa featuring interviews with Japanese Minister Yoshiatsu Murakami and Lima Nippo editor Choko Shinjo. Minister Murakami discounted the coup's international significance and denied war threats with Russia or the U.S., while Shinjo provided details on the assassinations and interpreted the rebellion as a nationalist-socialist uprising against corrupt party politicians.
subfiles.title: Lima Despatch on Japanese Legation Reactions in Peru

subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum criticizing Ambassador Saito's economic explanation of the assassinations as overly simplistic.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE: SKH:CC/REK)
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck rejects Saito's 'easy' agrarian-protest explanation, stressing deep army chauvinism and public tolerance of assassination as the real drivers aimed at removing civilian restraints.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Ambassador Saito's Explanation

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Phillips transmits memoranda regarding Hull's conversation with Saito and FE comments to Grew.
subfiles.summary: Phillips sends Grew copies of Hull's Saito conversation memo and Hornbeck's critique of the assassinations' causes.
subfiles.title: State Department Instruction to Tokyo Transmitting Saito Memoranda

subfiles.about: Consul Gilbert reports League Secretariat reactions and T. V. Soong's private claims of pre-planned Japanese demands on China.
subfiles.summary: Gilbert reports League Secretariat alarm over the coup; an official disclosed Soong's claim Japan's new China ambassador had prior instructions to demand North China autonomy and Manchukuo recognition.
subfiles.title: Geneva Despatch No. 1605 on League Reactions to Coup

subfiles.about: Grew reports extensive conference with Hirota regarding foreign policy, Soviet relations, and the three-point China program.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports an interview with newly appointed Prime Minister Hirota, who pledged continuity in foreign policy, ruled out war with the Soviet Union, and outlined his three-point program for China (anti-communist cooperation, suppression of anti-Japanese activity, and factual relations with Manchukuo). Hirota affirmed respect for the Open Door, while Grew informally raised U.S. domestic concerns over surging cheap Japanese imports. Paraphrases and a circular summary to Moscow are appended on pages 346-349.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 74 on Interview with Prime Minister Hirota

subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum evaluating Hirota's appointment as Premier and its probable impact on China policy.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE: SKH/ZMK)
subfiles.summary: Memo: Hirota, acceptable to the military and committed to his China program, was chosen by the Emperor/Saionji to reconcile factions while likely pursuing a more positive China policy.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Hirota as Premier and China Policy

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a China despatch enclosing a newspaper editorial on Sino-Russo-Japanese relations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Lockhart's despatch encloses a Peking/Tientsin Times editorial on China's dilemma between Japan and Russia.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Sino-Russo-Japanese Relations Editorial

subfiles.about: Grew reports public and military criticism of the newly issued Hirota Cabinet policy statement.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the Hirota Cabinet's policy declaration was widely criticized by press and military as vague and lacking concrete reforms.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 75 on Cabinet Statement of Policy

subfiles.about: Embassy Berlin transmits German Foreign Office-inspired Berliner Tageblatt editorial on the internal agrarian causes of the Tokyo coup.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Dodd forwards an editorial from the Berliner Tageblatt ('Zu den Ereignissen in Japan' / 'No Putsch') based on insights from a German Foreign Office Far East expert, accompanied by an FE covering memo. The article argues that the Tokyo rebellion stemmed primarily from internal economic misery and peasant distress rather than foreign expansionism, noting that the young officers reflect the suffering of their peasant troops.
subfiles.title: Berlin Despatch No. 2703 Transmitting German Press Editorial

subfiles.about: Embassy Paris transmits French newspaper articles and editorials analyzing the Tokyo military coup.
subfiles.summary: Embassadorial report transmitting French press coverage of the Tokyo coup from Excelsior, L'Echo de Paris (Pertinax), and La Republique (Pierre Brossolette), accompanied by an FE covering note. The French articles emphasize the clash between moderate parliamentarians and radical young military officers, analyzing Japanese political violence in terms of social unrest, patriotic secret societies, and the threat of aggressive expansion in Asia.
subfiles.title: Paris Transmission of French Press Clippings on Tokyo Coup
